name: Adobe Commerce Cloud
description: Adobe Commerce Cloud provides enterprise storefront, catalog, inventory, pricing, customer, order, promotion, and integration capabilities across Adobe Commerce cloud deployment models.
agentUseSummary: Adobe documents materially different REST endpoints and authentication for Commerce on Cloud PaaS and Commerce as a Cloud Service SaaS. Relay mounts no connection or tools until the customer identifies one deployment model, exact API origin and tenant, bounded commerce resource, and least-privilege service credential.

providerSetup.blocker: The generic provider name does not identify Adobe Commerce on Cloud PaaS versus Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service SaaS; Adobe documents different endpoint structures, available APIs, and authentication models for them.
providerSetup.nextAction: Record the exact Commerce deployment model. For SaaS, record the Adobe-provided API endpoint, server/tenant identifiers, store scope, and least-privilege IMS server-to-server product profile; for PaaS, record the exact HTTPS store origin and a narrowly scoped Commerce integration. Then select one bounded read-only resource and complete security review before mounting any connection or tool.

evidence.supports: Adobe explicitly distinguishes PaaS and SaaS Commerce REST APIs, documents different endpoint structures and available endpoints, and states PaaS uses OAuth 1.0a/tokens while SaaS uses IMS.
Adobe documents IMS OAuth server-to-server authentication for Commerce as a Cloud Service, requiring Developer Console, an organization admin, client credentials, and organization identity.
Adobe documents PaaS third-party integrations using store-specific OAuth 1.0a credentials, activation callbacks, long-lived access tokens, and resource permissions.
Adobe publishes separate PaaS and SaaS REST references, confirming that a generic Commerce Cloud contract cannot assume one common resource surface.
